function.name: game_scores_get
function.description: Retrieve scores and rankings based on player’s performance in a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

platform.description: The gaming platform e.g. Xbox, Playstation, PC

level.description: The level of the game for which you want to retrieve the scores.

player.description: The name of the player for whom you want to retrieve scores. Default ''

function.name: game_rewards_get
function.description: Retrieve information about different types of rewards that you can receive when playing a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

platform.description: The gaming platform e.g. Xbox, Playstation, PC

mission.description: The mission for which you want to know the rewards. Default to ''

trophy.description: The trophy level for which you want to know the rewards. Default to ''

function.name: game_missions_list
function.description: List all missions for a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
User wants to find rewards for different missions in Fortnite on PlayStation. We need to call game_rewards_get with game="Fortnite", platform="Playstation", mission maybe unspecified? They want "different missions and rewards". So we can list missions first using game_missions_list, then get rewards for each mission. But maybe just call game_rewards_get with mission unspecified to get all rewards? The function signature: game_rewards_get(game, platform, mission?, trophy?). We can call with mission='' to get all? The user says "尋找在Playstation平台上玩Fortnite時不同任務和獎益的獎勵." Means "Looking for rewards for different missions and benefits when playing Fortnite on PlayStation." So we should provide a list of missions and their rewards. Let's first get missions list. Then for each mission, get rewards. But we might not have many missions; maybe we can just call game_rewards_get with mission='' to get all rewards. But better to show missions and rewards.

We can call game_missions_list first.
